## 🚀 Background Description

Idea Tree works in the browser but has **no surface at all in the desktop app**: a desktop user can start a research from the composer and then has nowhere to watch it, pause it or read its nodes. This issue records what Idea Tree supports today and asks for a deliberately small desktop adaptation (settings pane + session panel + tree view), not a port of the web canvas.

### What Idea Tree supports today (verified on main `1b09f3ea`, 2026-11-15)

**Engine.** Runs inside the existing evolve Python service (one ASGI worker); the API owns session auth, model proxying and usage recording. State is persisted by Python at `$SCIENCE_AGENT_DATA_DIR/idea-research/<projectId>/<sessionId>/<researchId>.json` (atomic replace, no model keys). Source: `docs/zh/developer-docs/idea-tree.md`.

**How a research starts.** `/idea-tree <task>` or `/idea-tree-team <task>` in the composer queues a run whose `enabledSkillIds` gains `idea-tree-team` (`services/api/src/runs/index.ts:3447-3449`; `services/api/src/idea-tree/queue.test.ts:88-99` asserts this run has `ideaTreeEnabled=false` and does not contact the tree service). The `idea-tree-team` skill (`skills/idea-tree-team/SKILL.md`) prepares objective, constraints and materials, then calls the tool `create_idea_research(objective, materials)` (`packages/evolve/src/index.ts:443`). The engine then runs independently of the chat turn.

**Loop and limits.** Rounds of `ideation → design → independent activity/stability/sustainability assessment → aggregation → insight propagation`; default 3 rounds × 3 candidates, additionally bounded by max nodes, max depth and a token budget; assessor weights must sum to 1.0. Phases surface as `preflight_research`, `building_tree`, `executing_leaf`, `aggregating_score`, `propagating_insight`. Pause does not cancel in-flight model calls; after a process restart status becomes `interrupted` and is not auto-resumed; end keeps results and cannot continue. Legacy trees stay read-only.

**HTTP surface (all already public).**

| Endpoint | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET` / `PUT /api/settings/idea-tree` | defaults: template, intensity, budgets, score direction, role prompts, assessor prompts/weights (`services/api/src/http/index.ts:1951-1958`) |
| `GET /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research` | list this session's researches |
| `POST /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research` | `operation` ∈ `list, get, create, pause, continue, end, defaults` (`:4091-4107`); `create` with `content` also appends a user + assistant message to the session (`:4100-4102`) |
| `GET /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research/:id/events` | SSE progress stream (`:4073-4089`) |
| `GET /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/graph?tree_id=` | legacy tree graph, read-only (`:4109-4128`) |

**Data shapes.** `IdeaResearchState` carries `status` (`running / pausing / paused / interrupted / completed / ended`), `phase`, `round`, `batch`/`batchCompleted`, `tokens`, `usageKnown`, `activities[]`, frozen `settings` and `template` (`packages/schema/src/idea-tree.ts:289-323`). `IdeaTreeGraph` is `{ treeId, objective, revision, updatedAt, nodes[], edges[] }` (`:243-250`) and each node carries `kind` (direction/candidate), `depth`, `status`, `searchStatus`, `hypothesis`, `insight`, `result`, `stages`, `score`, `pruneReason`, `priority`, `attemptCount`, `artifactRefs[]`, `subagentIds[]` (`:105-129`).

**Web surfaces to mirror.** `IdeaTreeView` is the session panel, mounted only when the evolve sidecar is ready (`apps/web/src/App.tsx:5849`); it shows either the autonomous card (`IdeaResearchCard.tsx`, with pause/continue/end at `:83-87`) or the legacy tree summary. `IdeaTreeExplorer` is the dialog: SVG canvas (`IdeaTreeCanvas.tsx`), status filter chips, hypothesis search, node detail with artifact/subagent buttons. Settings live in `IdeaTreeSettingsEditor.tsx` under the `idea-tree` group. `IdeaResearchTimelineCard.tsx` shows progress inside a run timeline.

### What the desktop has today

- `apps/desktop/src/api/settings.ts:449-458` already wraps `GET`/`PUT /api/settings/idea-tree`, and `apps/desktop/src/text/{en,zh}.ts` already carries `settings.ideaTree.*` copy (template, intensity, budgets, prompts, assessors) — **nothing consumes either**. A grep for `idea-tree|IdeaTree|ideaTree` over `apps/desktop/src` returns only those three files.
- No research client, no SSE subscription, no panel, no entry: so a research started from the desktop composer is invisible, uncontrollable and unreadable there.
- The pieces to build it from already exist: SSE through `ApiClient.fetchStream` (`apps/desktop/src/api/client.ts:82`), an evolve subsystem to mirror (`app/evolve/use-evolve.ts`, `views/evolve/*`, mounted as the 任务 group's content in `App.tsx:1075`), workspace groups `PanelGroup = "artifacts" | "files" | "task"` (`views/WorkspacePanel.tsx:42`), the SessionBar action strip (`views/SessionBar.tsx:100-119`), and settings groups (`views/SystemSettingsDialog.tsx:33-54`).

### One contract question to settle

`docs/zh/developer-docs/idea-tree.md:26` says sending an Idea Tree command through the chat message API returns a `409` that redirects to the research entry ("不会悄悄启动 Lead"), but the code queues a normal run carrying the `idea-tree-team` skill, and its test asserts no tree-service call happens at queue time. Desktop copy and the entry hint depend on which behaviour is current.

## Design Ideas

Keep it small: one settings pane, one session panel, a simple indented tree instead of the SVG canvas, and no new start form (starting stays agent-driven, as the skill states: "Objective and prepared materials are backend inputs, not a separate front-end form").

**1. Settings pane (reuse what is already there).** Add `"idea-tree"` to `SettingsGroup` and to the `intelligence` category (`views/SystemSettingsDialog.tsx:33-54`), and render a pane that reads/writes the existing endpoints with the existing text keys: template, exploration intensity, rounds, candidates per round, max depth, max nodes, max search rounds, tokens per call, score direction, and the role/assessor prompts. Validate assessor weights sum to 1.0 client-side, as the web editor does, and surface the server message otherwise.

**2. Session panel.** A fourth right-panel group `"idea-tree"` next to 产物/工作区/任务, opened from a SessionBar toggle that mirrors the workspace toggle. The group is offered when the session has any research (`GET .../research` returns a non-empty list). Contents, in one column:

- research list: objective, status, round, tokens, updated time; selectable;
- current research summary: status/phase, round and batch progress, tokens (`usageKnown` decides whether the number or "unknown" is shown), last ~10 activities with role, node and duration;
- tree: an **indented, depth-grouped list** with the status colour, expand/collapse, a hypothesis search box and status filter chips (the mobile-friendly equivalent of the canvas);
- node detail: kind, depth, status/search status, hypothesis, insight, result where the web shows it, prune reason, assessment stages with scores, artifact refs → the existing artifact dialog, subagent ids → the existing `SubagentDetail`;
- controls: pause while `running`, continue while `paused`/`interrupted`, end behind a confirmation — same semantics as `IdeaResearchCard.tsx:83-87`.

**3. Live updates.** Subscribe to `.../research/:id/events` through `fetchStream` (the same shape as `subscribeEvolveEvents`), and fall back to polling the list on stream close so a dropped connection cannot freeze the panel. Refetch when the selected run or the session's message count changes, as the web panel does.

**4. Prerequisites, said out loud.** Research needs the evolve sidecar and a model with a token: the client throws `Evolve is not initialized...` (`services/api/src/idea-tree/research.ts:12`) and `Configure a model with an API token before starting research` (`:36`). Reuse `getEvolveStatus` (`api/evolve.ts:50`) so the panel offers the same "Init Evolve" affordance the desktop already has instead of a dead button.

**Out of scope:** the engine, the SVG canvas and score charts, legacy tree writes, materials upload, and any desktop form that creates a research directly.

## Involved Public APIs

Consumed only — nothing added, changed or removed:

- `GET` / `PUT /api/settings/idea-tree`
- `GET` / `POST /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research`
- `GET /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/research/:id/events` (SSE)
- `GET /api/sessions/:id/idea-tree/graph` (legacy trees, read-only)
- `GET /api/evolve/status` (sidecar gate)

If the panel later needs a server-side aggregate (for example per-research byte or token summaries), that is a separate additive change with its own issue.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

| Module | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/desktop/src/api/idea-tree.ts` (new) | research list/command/events, reusing `fetchStream` |
| `apps/desktop/src/app/use-idea-research.ts` (new) | hook mirroring `app/evolve/use-evolve.ts` |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/idea-tree/*` (new) | panel, tree list, node detail, controls |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/{SystemSettingsDialog,WorkspacePanel,SessionBar,App}.tsx` | settings group, panel group, entry, mounting |
| `apps/desktop/src/text/{zh,en}.ts` | the existing `settings.ideaTree.*` keys become live; new panel copy in both languages |
| `apps/web` | unchanged; its components define the behaviour to mirror |
| `packages/schema` | no change; `IdeaResearchView` / `IdeaTreeGraph` are already exported |
| `docs` | the chat-command contract question above needs one authoritative statement |

## Test Design and Test Plan

- **Component**: settings pane renders and validates weights; panel renders list/summary/detail; tree list search and status filters; pause/continue/end call the right operations; evolve-not-ready state; server error text shown inline; zh-CN and en.
- **Client**: research list/command parsing; SSE frame handling and the polling fallback when the stream closes.
- **E2E on the desktop build with the local stack**: start a research from the composer (`/idea-tree ...`), watch the panel reach a terminal state; pause → continue → end with confirmation; restart the app and reopen the panel (state comes from the server, not component memory); open an artifact and a subagent from a node.
- Commands: `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`, `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop build`, `pnpm ci:l1`.
- Screenshots (settings pane, running research, tree with node detail, paused state, evolve-not-ready state) go in the PR body for the owner's approval.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Desktop settings has an Idea Tree pane that reads and writes `/api/settings/idea-tree`, rejects assessor weights that do not sum to 1.0, and still shows them after a restart.
- [ ] The session surface lists that session's researches with objective, status, round and tokens, and survives a restart.
- [ ] Selecting a research shows its nodes as a simple indented tree with status colours, a hypothesis search and status filters, plus a node detail with hypothesis/insight/result/prune reason/stages/artifacts/subagents.
- [ ] Pause, continue and end behave like the web (`pausing` waits for in-flight calls, end asks for confirmation) and are disabled where the status makes them meaningless.
- [ ] Progress arrives without a manual reload (SSE, falling back to polling), and the panel never claims a status it did not read.
- [ ] When the evolve sidecar is not ready, or no model has an API token, the panel says so and offers the next step instead of failing silently.
- [ ] zh-CN and en copy; `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop typecheck|test|build` and `pnpm ci:l1` pass.
- [ ] The owner has seen the screenshots in the PR body before approval.

## Additional Information

Verified by reading, on main `1b09f3ea`: `packages/schema/src/idea-tree.ts`, `services/api/src/http/index.ts` (routes cited above), `services/api/src/idea-tree/{research,queue.test}.ts`, `services/api/src/runs/index.ts`, `packages/evolve/src/index.ts:443`, `skills/idea-tree-team/SKILL.md`, `apps/web/src/{IdeaTreeView,IdeaTreeExplorer,IdeaTreeCanvas,IdeaResearchCard,IdeaTreeSettingsEditor}.tsx`, `apps/web/src/App.tsx`, `docs/zh/developer-docs/idea-tree.md`.

Desktop gap verified by grep: `idea-tree|IdeaTree|ideaTree` over `apps/desktop/src` matches only `api/settings.ts`, `api/types.ts` and `text/{en,zh}.ts`; nothing renders or calls a research endpoint.

Requested by the user as: they need to review what Idea Tree currently supports and have the desktop client do a simple adaptation of the feature.

## Detailed Description of the Problem

The desktop conversation shows “Skipped 1 event this version does not recognise” when the API sends a valid `mcp.readiness` event. Users see the same notice when reopening an affected conversation. The desktop transcript discards the connector diagnostic, while the web timeline already renders it.

Minimal reproduction against the desktop run-stream reducer:

```ts
const state = reduceRunStream(emptyRunStream(), {
  type: "mcp.readiness",
  summary: "example: degraded; omitted tools: search.",
}, 1);
```

On main, `state.unknownEvents` is 1. To reproduce through the UI, run a desktop conversation with a selected MCP connector that is unavailable or degraded, then reopen the conversation and inspect the run. The desktop instead should keep the diagnostic in the run details and reserve the unknown-event notice for genuinely unrecognized events.

## 🚀 Background Description

Users need a research session exported to a `.sdresearch` package and imported again to retain its Evolve history. In a Windows desktop test, after exporting a session with a completed Evolve search, importing it and choosing to continue the research, the conversation no longer showed the interactive Evolve card or the task panel containing the optimization results.

This request covers the complete user-facing preservation and acceptance of Evolve history across export, import and creation of a writable research continuation. Related: #1019 addressed the earlier absence of Evolve run records in research packages; #1060 and #1136 added run/event and candidate-source packaging. Draft PR #1176 addresses run-ID collisions during import and continuation; its desktop journey and full validation remain outstanding.

## Design Ideas

- Carry each selected session's Evolve runs, configuration, budget, status, events, candidate tree, scores, best result and available candidate source content in the package, for both supported export levels.
- Restore each run under the correct imported session. Repeated imports, importing on the source machine, and creating a writable continuation must produce independent, correctly associated records without overwriting another session's runs or mixing candidates.
- In both the read-only imported snapshot and the writable continuation, show the Evolve card and allow it to open the desktop task panel. Preserve the optimization tree, budget and results, node selection, candidate details and available source/diff views.
- Preserve multiple runs and their ownership. Report missing or omitted run data, events or candidate sources explicitly, while keeping the rest of the session usable. Older packages cannot recover data they never contained.
- Do not automatically restart a search when importing or viewing it. An in-flight search cannot continue on the target merely from a historical snapshot: present a truthful historical/terminal state and retain available partial results. Access to a still-running source session remains a separate live status, not an imported live execution.
- Re-running a search or achieving identical scientific results in another environment is outside this request.

## Involved Public APIs

Prefer the existing session export/import and research-continuation APIs and the Evolve run-list, event and candidate-source read APIs. Verify their behavior with remapped run IDs and session ownership; document any necessary additive contract or compatibility changes. Import must not execute package contents.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

Research package serialization, validation, import and continuation; Evolve run/event storage and candidate source storage; session ownership and ID mapping; desktop conversation cards, task panel, tree and node inspector. Preserve compatibility with old packages and sessions without Evolve.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- Add regression coverage for completed, stopped, failed and in-flight searches, multiple runs, missing candidate sources, malformed package data and sessions without Evolve.
- Export and import on the source machine and a fresh data directory; repeat the import and create a writable continuation. Check independent ownership, run identifiers, event order, budgets, scores, candidate content, and absence of automatic execution.
- Exercise the actual Windows desktop user journey: complete a search → export → import → open the card and task panel → inspect tree nodes and source/diff → continue research → repeat the inspection. Also verify the imported snapshot remains read-only and the new session supports chat.
- Run the applicable unit, system and mocked E2E gates (`pnpm ci:ut`, `pnpm ci:st`, `pnpm ci:e2e`) and report counts; distinguish blocked environment checks from passing results.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After export and import, each Evolve run is associated with the right session and its interactive card opens the task panel, including optimization results, tree, budgets, scores and available node details and source/diff.
- [ ] Creating a writable research continuation preserves the same available Evolve history and allows subsequent chat; the imported snapshot stays read-only.
- [ ] Same-machine import, repeated import and multiple Evolve runs retain independent, correctly associated records without overwriting the original or mixing sources.
- [ ] Stopped, failed and previously running searches display truthful status and available partial data; viewing or importing never starts a new search.
- [ ] Missing or omitted data and limitations of older packages are reported explicitly, and the rest of the session remains usable.
- [ ] Relevant automated regression and Windows desktop user-journey checks pass, with command results and any remaining limitations recorded.

## Additional Information

The requested behavior is preservation and inspection of recorded Evolve results, not deterministic reproduction or automatic resumption. PR #1176 is a draft and must not be treated as full desktop validation.

## Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] Please note that if your bug description lacks corresponding environment information and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be difficult for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, which will reduce the possibility of receiving feedback, or even lead to the issue being closed.

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

Four tests in `application/test` assume POSIX capabilities that a stock Windows 11 host does not have, so `pnpm --dir application test` (and therefore the Windows installer build) is red on such a machine even though the product code is fine. They pass on the CI `windows-latest` runner (see Additional Information), which is why this only shows up for people packaging the Windows app locally.

Running `pnpm --dir application test` on a stock Windows 11 host (Node 22.23.4) gives `# tests 343 / # pass 339 / # fail 4`:

```
not ok 27 - dirWritable answers true for a writable dir and false for a read-only one
  location: 'application/test/bootstrap.test.ts:417:1'
  error: |-
    Expected values to be strictly equal:
    true !== false

not ok 28 - bootstrapPackaged degrades in-place to copy mode on a read-only payload (W16 DMG run)
  location: 'application/test/bootstrap.test.ts:434:1'
  error: |-
    Expected values to be strictly equal:
    true !== false

not ok 248 - uninstall-mac.command: syntax-clean under macOS bash 3.2 (bash -n)
  location: 'application/test/uninstall-data.test.ts:80:1'
  error: 'spawnSync /bin/bash ENOENT'

not ok 288 - replaceVenvSymlinks rewrites burned-in absolute targets to the relative bundled target
  location: 'application/test/venv-launchers.test.ts:102:1'
  error: "EPERM: operation not permitted, symlink 'C:\\Users\\builder\\.workbuddy\\...\\bin\\python3'
          -> 'C:\\Users\\...\\Temp\\sd-sym-...\\v\\bin\\python'"
```

Cause, one by one:

1. **`bootstrap.test.ts:417` / `:434`** — the fixture runs `chmod(dir, 0o555)` and expects `dirWritable()` to answer `false`. On NTFS `chmod` only toggles the read-only attribute and does not make a directory unwritable for its owner, so `dirWritable()` correctly answers `true`; the second test is the same assertion through `bootstrapPackaged`. Both describe a macOS DMG-mounted payload (`W16`), which cannot be simulated this way on Windows.
2. **`uninstall-data.test.ts:80`** — `execFileSync("/bin/bash", ["-n", SCRIPT])` needs a real `/bin/bash`, which a Windows host does not have (Git for Windows ships `bash.exe` elsewhere, WSL is not guaranteed, and the test should not depend on either).
3. **`venv-launchers.test.ts:102`** — `makePosixVenv()` creates symlinks; creating symlinks on Windows needs Developer Mode or elevation, so it raises `EPERM` on a default install.

Minimal reproduction (no test code needed):

```powershell
pnpm --dir application install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm --dir application test          # 339 pass, 4 fail on a stock Windows 11 host
```

Impact: `pnpm --dir application dist` is the command that produces the user-facing NSIS installer, and CI runs the same test step before it. Anyone who builds the installer on a normal Windows machine has to either ignore a red gate or hand-skip it; our Windows packaging job is currently blocked at exactly this gate.

## Detailed Environment Information Description

| | |
| --- | --- |
| OS | Microsoft Windows 11 家庭版 10.0.26200 (build 26200) |
| Node | v22.23.4 (x64) |
| pnpm | 11.1.2 |
| Shell used for the build | Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.9818 (non-interactive) |
| Electron workspace | `application/` (renamed from `win_desktop/` by the macOS adaptation) |
| Developer Mode | off; the process is not elevated |
| `bash` on PATH | none (`/bin/bash` absent; no Git Bash/MSYS exposure in this shell) |
| Test command | `pnpm --dir application test` (`node --experimental-strip-types --no-warnings --test test/*.test.ts`) |

## Additional Information

**CI does pass this step, which localises the problem to host capabilities rather than product code.** For commit `5058334f09a7b28c7c56dbbdb199b2adf13adf74`, Nightly run `43984975918`, job `Gate / Windows desktop installer` (`133716724096`, `windows-latest`): step 16 "Test and typecheck the desktop shell" = **success**; the job fails later, at step 17 "Build the Windows installer". The same job is skipped on `push` (`43886126438`) and `merge_group` (`43880862208`) because it is gated on `needs.policy.outputs.windows_desktop == 'true'` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:896`), so only the Nightly/release runs exercise it.

Suggested change — gate on the capability the test needs, not on a platform guess:

- `uninstall-data.test.ts:80`: skip when `/bin/bash` is not executable (`existsSync("/bin/bash")` or a `spawnSync` capability probe), and say in a comment that the macOS 3.2 syntax check only runs where that shell exists.
- `venv-launchers.test.ts:102`: skip when a symlink probe in the temp dir throws `EPERM`/`EACCES`, so a machine without Developer Mode still exercises the rest of the file.
- `bootstrap.test.ts:417` / `:434`: these two describe the macOS DMG payload; either skip them on `win32` (the payload is never read-only there) or replace the `chmod` fixture with a Windows-valid read-only simulation (an ACL that denies write) so the assertion means something on both hosts.

The four failures are test-only; `pnpm --dir application build`, `assemble` and `electron-builder --win` are unaffected once the gate is passed.

## Version Information

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Commit | `5058334f09a7b28c7c56dbbdb199b2adf13adf74` ("feat(mac): macOS desktop adaptation — shell, packaging chain, sandbox & distribution") |
| Desktop shell package | `sd-shell` 0.4.0 (`application/package.json`) |
| Electron | `^37.0.0` (declared in `application/package.json`) |
| Node | v22.23.4 |
| CI evidence | Nightly run `43984975918`, job `133716724096` |

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

The desktop session header has an Export button at the upper right while the session's sidebar menu already provides an export action. These duplicate entries add an unwanted persistent control to the session header.
